investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent 'BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 (+https://github.com/chriswatson6675/band_on_the_map)', no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official /events/ page, then against the WordPress REST API endpoint that page's own HTML directly links to (wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events) — both plain unauthenticated GETs, no escalation. The /events/ page's own <script type=application/ld+json> block already carries full schema.org Event data for the current week; the linked REST API (The Events Calendar / Events Calendar Pro plugin, the SAME generic family already proven for ccb-lisbon-01 and yaam-berlin-01) returns the venue's full 95-event schedule across 2 pages.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the official events page (https://supersonic-club.fr/events/) found a WordPress site running The Events Calendar / Events Calendar Pro (confirmed: 'tribe-events'/'tribe_events'/'wp-json/tribe/events/v1/' markup throughout) whose own <script type=application/ld+json> block already carries 7 full schema.org Event records (name/startDate/endDate/location/offers) for the current week. The same page's own static <a href> links (an 'Add to calendar' feature) directly advertise the plugin's own public REST API endpoint (https://supersonic-club.fr/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events) — a further plain, unauthenticated GET of that SAME publicly-linked endpoint returned the venue's full 95-event schedule across 2 pages, each event carrying id/title/start_date/utc_start_date/venue/cost/url directly. This fully answers the investigation question at Level 1 (a plain request, following the page's own advertised link, with no browser/JS/authentication); no structural/browser escalation was needed.

venue_reference: Supersonic (concert/club venue, 9 rue Biscornet, 75012 Paris — includes its sister room 'Supersonic Records', same operator, same address)

identity.notes: The retained events page's own JSON-LD 'location.name' states 'SUPERSONIC' directly, with a full postal address ('9 Rue Biscornet, Paris, 75012, France') and telephone matching this task's assigned address exactly, at the venue's own domain supersonic-club.fr. The REST API's own per-event 'venue' object independently confirms the same address for BOTH 'SUPERSONIC' and 'Supersonic Records' — a first-party confirmation that these are the same operator/building, per this task's own note, not two separate venues.

site_classification.platform: WordPress running The Events Calendar + Events Calendar Pro (confirmed: 'tribe-events-c-*' CSS classes, 'tribe_events' post-type-archive class, 'wp-json/tribe/events/v1/' and 'wp-json/tribe/views/v2/html' links, webcal:// ICS export links). The plugin's own bundled REST API v1 (https://supersonic-club.fr/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events) is public, unauthenticated, and directly linked from the plugin's own rendered HTML — the SAME generic family and acquisition path already proven for ccb-lisbon-01 (Lisbon) and yaam-berlin-01 (Berlin), requiring ZERO new collector code (ingestion/events-calendar-api/ + ingestion/events-calendar-api/observation-adapter.mjs, unmodified). The /events/ listing page's own JSON-LD is corroborating evidence, not the primary data path (it only exposes the current week's ~7 events, a date-windowed view; the REST API exposes the full 95-event schedule across 2 pages of 50).

title.notes: The REST API's own 'title' field (and the JSON-LD's own 'name' field, independently corroborating), stated directly.

start_date.notes: The REST API's own 'start_date' local field ('2026-08-27 19:00:00'), stated directly. IMPORTANT HONEST CAVEAT: this record ALSO carries a 'utc_start_date' field ('2026-08-27 18:00:00', a fixed 1-hour delta from local) and the JSON-LD's own 'startDate' states an explicit '+01:00' offset — but France observes Central European SUMMER Time (CEST, UTC+2) from late March to late October, so the TRUE correct UTC offset for a late-August date is +02:00, not +01:00. This source's own 'UTC'/offset computation therefore appears to use a FIXED, non-DST-aware offset rather than genuinely resolving 'Europe/Paris' with its seasonal rule — see collector_assessment.blockers. The calendar-DATE portion ('2026-08-27') is unaffected by this and remains fully PROVEN either way.

time.value: 19:00 (Europe/Paris local wall-clock time, as directly stated by the source's own 'start_date' field)
time.notes: Stated directly by the source's own local 'start_date' field. Recorded as the local wall-clock value, NOT as a confirmed UTC instant — see start_date's notes on this source's own apparently DST-unaware 'utc_start_date'/JSON-LD offset fields.

end.notes: The REST API's own 'end_date' field ('2026-08-27 23:00:00') and the JSON-LD's own 'endDate' ('2026-08-27T23:00:00+01:00') both directly state a same-day, 4-hour-later end time — a genuine performance end-time, not a Tempodrom-style 'last calendar day of a multi-day run' placeholder (confirmed across every sampled record: every end_date shares the same calendar day as its own start_date).

venue_location.value: SUPERSONIC / Supersonic Records, 9 Rue Biscornet, Paris, 75012, France
venue_location.notes: The REST API's own per-event 'venue' object directly states BOTH 'SUPERSONIC' and 'Supersonic Records' as venue names across the sampled 95-event schedule, but with the IDENTICAL address ('9 Rue Biscornet Paris 75012 France') in every case — confirming this task's own note that these are one operator/building sharing the same room, not two separate venues. Treated as a single canonical venue entity.

source_record_id.value: the record's own numeric WordPress post 'id'
source_record_id.notes: The REST API's own numeric 'id' field, the platform's own permanent primary-key identifier for its REST resource — a documented, stable platform convention (the same judgement already accepted for yaam-berlin-01). Not independently re-verified by a second fetch of the identical event within this investigation's bounded scope, but WordPress post IDs are a well-established stable platform identifier by design, not a value this investigation invented.

event_url.notes: The REST API's own 'url' field (and the JSON-LD's own 'url' field, independently corroborating), stated directly.

price.value: Gratuit (free) for the sampled record; other sampled records state e.g. '10€'
price.notes: The REST API's own 'cost' field is genuinely populated per-event (unlike most other WordPress-based sources this project has investigated, e.g. ccb-lisbon-01, where it is empty) — a real, complete, first-party price/free-entry statement.

blockers.description: This source's own 'utc_start_date'/'utc_end_date' fields (and the corresponding JSON-LD '+01:00' offset) do not appear to account for French Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2, in effect for this event's own late-August date) — comparing the same record's local 'start_date' ('2026-08-27 19:00:00') against its own 'utc_start_date' ('2026-08-27 18:00:00') shows a fixed 1-hour delta, i.e. this WordPress install's own timezone/UTC computation appears pinned to a fixed UTC+1 offset rather than genuinely resolving 'Europe/Paris' with its seasonal DST rule. Using this source's own utc fields as a genuinely confirmed UTC_INSTANT (the EXISTING ingestion/events-calendar-api/observation-adapter.mjs's default behaviour, already proven correct for ccb-lisbon-01/yaam-berlin-01) would silently misattribute a 1-hour error during DST months for THIS specific source. NOT CRITICAL — the local start_date/end_date fields remain fully reliable; the mitigation (documented, not applied, per this task's instruction not to edit shared generic modules) is for the eventual Paris wiring layer to omit/null this source's own utc_start_date/utc_end_date fields before calling the existing generic adapter (yielding FLOATING_LOCAL certainty from the local fields alone, which is correct) rather than trusting this source's own apparently-incorrect UTC arithmetic.
